content.comment_body: I have several projects using [product_name] base modules and expansion modules. Each base module includes multiple [product_name] expansion modules. The logic program operates from one base module, while another provides outputs through various network input function blocks. The base modules are networked with CAT5e cable. Occasionally, I encounter LAN issues where temporarily disconnecting the CAT5e cable or cycling power restores outputs on one of the base modules. Is this a known problem? Any suggestions for improving LAN reliability?

What is the length of the Cat5e cable? Have you considered potential interference from running the cable parallel to load circuits? Are both ground connections of the modules tied to ground potential? If so, try disconnecting one of those ground connections.

Appreciate the suggestions, [user_name]. The cable is about 30 inches (762mm) and runs inside the wire duct alongside several load wires. I will try a shorter cable and route it outside the duct, separated from the load wiring. I also plan to disconnect the ground on one of the base modules.
Looking forward to hearing the outcome. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing intermittent LAN communication issues between base and expansion modules in installations with [product_name]. These issues cause temporary output loss and are often resolved by reconnecting the network cable or restarting power. Discussions focus on cable management and minimizing electrical interference to improve network reliability and overall stability of the system.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect reliable and stable LAN connectivity between system modules, eliminating the need for manual intervention to restore communication. The system should maintain consistent output status and resist disruptions from minor disturbances.
